turns.speaker: Nidhi Hegde
turns.text: Okay. Privacy for— I mean, these different terms touch on different things. Privacy is really touching on privacy from the— when I'm talking about machine learning models, it touches on what can be inferred about an individual that they didn't want inferred, and that wasn't part of your original goal for that machine learning model. So maybe you're trying to recommend movies, but you are also able to infer their political views or sexual orientation. So that's a privacy matter. In the past, people have talked about privacy from the perspective of data privacy. How do I keep the actual data private? But now we're talking more about inferences and how these inferences can lead to privacy breaches. When it comes to fairness, it's really about the outcomes of these machine learning models, let's say predictions, that are then used for decision-making, and you get unfair outcomes across different subgroups. And you get that because your model has different error rates, for example, across different subgroups. So you might have different demographics that are in the population that your dataset is based on, and you may get different error rates. For example, image classification, maybe there's a higher error rate for Black women than there is for white men. So that's, that's unfairness. Robustness is really a more technical term about how robust your actual machine learning model is. And by— and when we say robust, we mean robust to shifts. So, for example, your data distribution has shifted. Maybe you've trained your data on— you've trained your model on data from 20 years ago, and the data distribution today looks different. You wanna build models that are robust to such shifts. So that's really what people talk about when they talk about robustness. Trust is really like the perspective of someone who's either using the model or the model is used on them, and you want them to be able to trust the model so that it is maybe private or maybe fair. You know, that really depends on the individual, like what they want to trust the model for.
